html:
Duwarkani / Prakheta (F62 → F64)

Survey-table region: Sarhal.

1444 starting country: Duwarkani (F62) Optional continuous formable: Prakheta (F64)

In one sentence: Duwarkani is a revival campaign in which humans and harpies inherit an ancient empire but reject its racial prejudice: through Nirakhet’s teaching that the Mother Weeps for All, you integrate gnolls, lizardfolk, gnomes, and trolls, suppress the Ahati revolt, cleanse the Shadow Swamp, and finally make the famed monster-slayer Castan Beastbane confront the crimes he committed.

Story: Extremely high | Mission-tree length: Medium (29 direct missions) | Mission-tree update: current local files updated through 2026-07-09 | Distinctiveness: Extremely high | Tedium: High | Early pressure: High | Expansion: Above average

Identity and History

Duwarkani (F62) is a small Nirakhetist kingdom in central Sarhal, at the edge of the Shadow Swamp. In 1444 it is a monarchy, primarily Tiariheti, and also accepts Nzeri Harpy culture. King Kenmu Menkaunswt is human and follows Elikhetism (the Mod’s religion key is elikhetist, with the English display “Elikhetist”), while Queen Safana and heir Banafriet are Nirakhetist harpies. It therefore begins not as a single-species country, but as a political community founded on a dynastic union between human and harpy royalty. [Local history script] [Current localisation]

The Menkaunswt family once ruled ancient Kheterata. The warrior-king Menkaunswt founded the Ahati and brought harpies into the army; later, the Crodamic dynasty exiled his descendants to Duwarkani. The 1444 history file explicitly lists Kenmu Menkaunswt, his Nzeri Harpy queen Safana, and their heir Banafriet, born in 1443 and inheriting the Menkaunswt name and Nzeri culture. This establishes the union of human and harpy royal houses, but does not establish the marriage date or the exact year Munzesh was annexed. [Local history script] [Local flavour text] [Wiki]

Nirakhetism is the country’s moral core. The offline Wiki says that Nirakhet worship was long popular among Kheterata’s lower classes and developed into a distinct faith among the Nzeri harpies; its central image is the Mother weeping for every life lost. Duwarkani takes this doctrine to its political limit: any rational being should be mourned, protected, and treated as a member of the community, and “monster” is no longer a legitimate racial category. [Wiki] [Local flavour text]

National Story and Campaign Arc

The opening is a crisis of survival and succession. Caught between powerful neighbours, mages, and the Shadow Swamp, Duwarkani must build the Shadow Dam, secure Samsumbat, and arrange a royal marriage. Kenmu and Safana are then assassinated by opponents of interspecies marriage; their harpy heir succeeds them, and the country becomes the “Winged Menkaunswt” diarchy. [Local missions] [Local events]

The second phase is to reclaim the Sadra and rebuild the Ahati. You must retake Kheterata’s core, become Guardian of the Sadra, and transform the Ahati from an order that excluded non-human peoples into an open military and political network. Reform angers the old brotherhood and triggers a long, highly destructive Ahati disaster. After suppressing the revolt, the bronze dragon Aakhet appears, reveals that he is the ancient warrior-king Menkaunswt, and recognises the winged heir’s strength and legitimacy. [Local missions] [Local events] [Local disaster script]

The country incorporates each people into its institutions: harpy standard-bearers, gnome mages, gnoll caravans, lizardfolk architects, and troll Ahati. The endgame requires high tolerance and acceptance of these cultures, turning conquest, conversion, estates, and the army into a single integration project. [Local missions]

The final arc enters the Shadow Swamp and the Shadowrealm. You break the hags’ control of the World Tree, discover that Shadow Trolls are not inherently evil tools, and find Castan II “Beastbane,” who had disappeared there. This famous monster-slayer gradually sees that every people he killed flows into the same river of the dead. When he asks, “Would Nirakhet weep for someone like me?”, Duwarkani’s national ideal receives its strongest proof: forgiveness does not deny wrongdoing, but refuses to keep producing it through permanent racial labels. [Local events]

Core Mechanics

Human administration and harpy armies. The country begins under human royalty but transitions to harpy rule; it retains human cavalry, creating an unusual combined force of flying troops, cavalry, and Ahati. [Local history script] [Official development diary]

Ahati reform and disaster. Opening the brotherhood unlocks privileges for different peoples but may trigger an old-guard revolt. The disaster severely damages trade, tax, production, and morale, and can even prohibit declaring war; it is the campaign’s largest “tedium” point. [Local missions] [Local disaster script]

Institutions unlocked by people. Gnolls support commerce, gnomes craft orbs, lizardfolk contribute to construction, and trolls join the Ahati. Missions also require cultural acceptance and racial tolerance, so conquest alone is not enough. [Local missions]

Paladins and protective magic. The “Magical Edict” requires magic to protect the people. Anti-ballistic amulets, frontier fortresses, the Shadow Dam, and paladins shape a defensive and damage-mitigation playstyle. [Local missions] [Local flavour text]

Shadow expedition and Beastbane’s ending. Swamp cleansing, the World Tree, hags, Shadow Troll origins, and Beastbane’s spirits form a continuous exploration arc. Beyond its rewards, it directly rewrites the traditional story of a “hero who slays monsters,” making this the tree’s most distinctive element. [Local events]

Play by Phase

Survive the opening: Secure Samsumbat, use the mountains, forts, and mercenaries to find weaker targets. Securing the gold mine, weakening mage neighbours, or building strategic depth is generally more reliable than mechanically following mission claims.

Succession and the northern advance: Put the harpy heir on the throne, complete the diarchy, and then advance north along the Sadra. Prepare religion, cultural acceptance, and racial tolerance together.

The Ahati crisis: Prepare for the disaster after rebuilding the brotherhood. Low mandate, low loyalty, and separatist tendencies accelerate collapse; stockpile money, manpower, and stability in advance.

The swamp and endgame: Integrate lizardfolk to the southeast, bring trolls into the state from the Shadow Swamp, and cleanse the World Tree to complete the institutions for five peoples. The later expansion is not global conquest, but it is geographically scattered and requires simultaneous attention to conversion, construction, and cultural acceptance.

Formables and Ending

Duwarkani has two formable choices that are easy to confuse. The decision to form Prakheta (F64) explicitly says that it retains the missions and does not call a mission-swap effect, so it can serve as a continuous Tag change at the end of the F62 campaign; it changes national ideas but does not add a new mission tree. Forming Kheterata (U01), by contrast, explicitly calls swap_non_generic_missions and switches to Kheterata content. This is an optional route away from Duwarkani’s campaign arc; it is best considered after completing this tree. [Local formation decisions]

Duwarkani’s own true ending is not a Tag change, but the answer to the question “Even for you?”: all major peoples become children of Nirakhet, the Shadow Swamp is freed from the hags, the Ahati accepts a multi-ethnic order, and Beastbane finally acknowledges that he treated his victims as soulless monsters.

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 76/100 | Autocracy 55/100 | Magic↔Artifice 85/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 72/100) | Pluralism 95/100.

The v2.1 values assessment is Good (94/100), with an improving trajectory. The route institutionalises the inclusion of humans, harpies, gnolls, lizardfolk, gnomes, and trolls, and emphasises protecting civilians, repentance, and forgiveness. It is among the strongest examples of universal personhood in the current sample.

Recommended for players who enjoy strong narrative, a difficult small-country opening, harpy military, multi-ethnic integration, religious idealism, and Shadowrealm exploration. Not recommended if you dislike estate privileges, an economy crippled during disasters, cultural or religious requirements, or a tree that ends before world conquest in 1821.

Community Experience

[Community view] A 2025 strategy discussion treats the opening as the most dangerous stage and recommends using terrain, alliances, the gold mine, and magic-resource sites to establish a position before claiming Guardianship. Players also warn that the Ahati disaster can damage the economy for a long time, though they disagree on the order of wars.

[Community view] Another story-focused recommendation praises Duwarkani’s treatment of Beastbane and the idea of “monsters,” while criticising the abrupt ending and irrevocable estate privileges that hinder absolutism. A comment adds that some absolutism penalties disappear late in the mission tree. This records player experience, not a substitute for current script conditions.

Evidence Boundaries

This article concerns the local Mod and translation for v1.37.5.0; the evidence page records a verification date of 2026-09-23. F62’s identity, 29 direct missions, F64’s mission retention, U01’s mission swap, the Ahati disaster, species integration, and the Beastbane ending are drawn from current local files.

The offline Wiki has no dedicated Duwarkani country page. This article uses only Nirakhet (page_id=2235, revision_id=32108), Aakhet the Bronze (382/31416), and Ahati (2683/20360) for religious and historical context. Full records for the official development diary, release announcement, and two player sources are on the evidence page.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Duwarkani (F62) — Duwarkani Ideas

Set ID: F62_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = F62
    }

Duwarkani Traditions

  • Number of accepted cultures: +2 (num_accepted_cultures; raw value 2).

  • Fort defense: +15% (defensiveness; raw value 0.15).

1. Feathers of Ma'at

The Upholders of Ma'at were a holy order of harpy warriors whose mission was to guard the khetist faithful who ventured away from the Sorrow. Most of the order died at the hands of Grizaka's army during the siege of Golkora, but a small chapter survived in Duwarkani and refounded themselves as the Feathers of Ma'at to commemorate the martyred bodies of their sisters.

  • Army morale: +10% (land_morale; raw value 0.1).

2. Land of Red Camels

Duwarkani is known for its hardy herdsmen and their distinctive red-furred camels. This local breed is well suited to the rocky and treacherous terrain of the mountainsides and the sparse forage found there. Duwarkani men are often away from home for months, driving the camels to foraging spots while hunting game from atop their mounts. The skill with which these men handle their animals and the capabilities of the breed make them fierce opponents in the twisting valleys and ravines, appearing at will from behind hills and crags to pour arrow-fire into the enemy.

  • Cavalry combat ability: +15% (cavalry_power; raw value 0.15).

3. Oversee the Faithful

Duwarkani is the southern outpost of the khetist faith. Responsible for guarding Kheterata from lizardfolk incursions and ensuring the safety of pilgrims traveling through Khetapera. Now that Grizaka's war has sundered the empire, this mission remains. Protect the faithful. Guard Kheterata. Guide the pilgrims.

  • Missionaries: +1 (missionaries; raw value 1).

4. Hanging Gardens

The wives and daughters of the Duwarkani’s villages maintain large gardens built into the mountainsides. They compete with each other to display the wealth of their village through gaudy arrangements of flowers and carved heads that trumpet a village's name and wealth to distant travelers or rivals the valley over. There is no sight more beloved in Duwarkani than to glimpse one’s garden after a long journey.

  • Prestige decay: -1% (prestige_decay; raw value -0.01).

  • National tax modifier: +5% (global_tax_modifier; raw value 0.05).

5. The Blood of Menkaunswt

The greatest Steward in all of Kheterata’s long history started life as a simple Irsmahapan soldier. Serving at a time when Kheterata was forced to kowtow to the upstart slaves in Castanor, Menkaunswt’s many successes would see him rise through the ranks at an unprecedented speed, until he could depose the traitorous Steward and reclaim Kheterata’s pride. His 65 year-long reign would see the Castanorians pushed back, Akasik and much of Bulwar subjugated, a bloom in relations with the Hierarchy, the birth of the Ahati and Kheteratan gem magic, and the integration of the Delta Gnomes and Nzeri Harpies into Kheteratan society.

While the rule of Menkaunswt’s dynasty ended with the Damerian invasion, his name still carried enough power that the Crodamic rulers saw fit to banish what remained of the family to most remote part of Kheterata they could think of: the distant fortress city at the very edge of the Shadow Swamp, known as Duwarkani. Here his descendants still rule, heirs to a lineage surpassed only by the khet themselves!

  • True faith tolerance: +2 (tolerance_own; raw value 2).

6. Union of Royalty

Humans and harpies have long lived side by side in Duwarkani, with the human governors and harpy matriarchs each ruling their respective peoples in the name of the Stewards. But with the authority of Kheterata gone, and no Stewards to command governor and matriarch, both sides agreed that a closer union was needed to ensure a united leadership of Duwarkani. With the marriage of Lord Kenmu and Lady Safana, the dynasty of Menkausnwt and the Duwaran dynasty which has ruled the Nzeri since the year 600 have now united into one. Thus was born an heir worthy to rule all of Duwarkani, and perhaps even all of Kheterata...

  • Stability cost modifier: -15% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.15).

7. Spotters and Camel Gunners

Lightly equipped harpy targeters combined with camel mounted heavy guns allow the armies of Duwarkani to turn the mountains into deathtraps. The harpies mark their targets with thrown burning alchemical flares or pots of colored dust, prompting the fire of the battery on priority targets.

  • Cavalry Fire: +50% (cavalry_fire; raw value 0.5).

Duwarkani Ambitions

  • global_manpower_modifier: +15% (global_manpower_modifier; raw value 0.15).

Prakheta (F64) — Prakhetan Ideas

Set ID: F64_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = F64 #Prakheta
    }

Prakhetan Traditions

  • Fort defense: +15% (defensiveness; raw value 0.15).

  • Goods produced modifier: +10% (global_trade_goods_size_modifier; raw value 0.1).

1. A New Kheterata

Once, the Crodamic dynasty were the grandest servants of the Khet, showing the light of the Khet for the very first time to the people of Khetapera and Horashesh. But even the most illustrious dynasties can fall to decadence, and the Crodamics were sadly no different. Stewards wasted men in petty wars with Bulwari and Cannorians while the forces of evil and corruption were waiting right outside their borders, secluded High Priests proclaimed stiff doctrines with no regard for the common worshipper, and the most holy Khetarch Baqtkhet I’s decision to promise the crown to Jaher led to centuries of heathens claiming ownership over Kheterata. Our new kingdom is a chance to start fresh again, with a government that understands the true needs of the land and its people. May it not repeat the mistakes of the past.

  • Yearly corruption: -0.1 (yearly_corruption; raw value -0.1).

2. The Source of the Sorrow

The Stewards of the Sorrow have traditionally ruled from the great city of Kheterat, reportedly built by Elikhet himself near the ruins of a genie city. Yet there can be no holier city than Niramit, located at the very Source of the Mother’s Sorrow, the birthplace of the great river that gives life to Kheterata and even to the Khet themselves. Beyond the city’s religious significance, its simultaneous location on the shores of both the Mother’s Sorrow and Lake Nirakhet does wonders for our administration’s ability to send people to and from every corner of our kingdom on a good timeframe.

  • True faith tolerance: +2 (tolerance_own; raw value 2).

  • Manpower recovery speed: +5% (manpower_recovery_speed; raw value 0.05).

3. Lessons from the Khetaperan Wars

As the demonic gnolls of Gnollakaz invaded Irsmahap and most of the southern nobility was slaughtered in battle, the cities of Khetapera were both cut off from the central authority of Kheterata and bereft of the region’s traditional ruling class. Left to fend for themselves, the different cities started waging war on each over their different visions for what rule of the region should look like. These wars carried unique difficulties due to the many mountain fortifications across the region. Learning how to siege these mountain forts and maneuvering through the narrow mountain passes that they guard have given our generals unmatched skill in besting the difficult conditions of this region.

  • Siege ability: +5% (siege_ability; raw value 0.05).

  • Land leader maneuver: +1 (leader_land_manuever; raw value 1).

4. Holding Back the Darkness

The forces of evil are ever at our doorstep. In the savannah, the gnolls prepare their sacrificial pyres for their infernal masters. In the swamp, the hags plot their schemes with troll slave and human pawn alike. The Crodamics failed to truly understand the threat of the darkness at their borders, and it ultimately cost them everything. We must never repeat their grave mistake. Our soldiers must always be ready to keep the forces of chaos at bay, and our rulers must never forget what is at stake should they lapse in their focus.

  • shock_damage_received: -15% (shock_damage_received; raw value -0.15).

5. Elikhet’s Decree on Magic

Elikhet’s Decree on Magic is possibly the most widely interpreted and debated of all his decrees. While everyone after the end of the Damerian Occupation and Elikhet’s Return would agree that the Decree stresses the importance of the mages to use their divine gift for the benefit of the Khet and Kheterata instead of corrupting it for their own selfish desires, the specifics on how to enforce it varies wildly. The Decree has been used as justification for stripping mages of their freedom and turning them into bound labor, investing vast powers and privileges to a magical oversight committee staffed by the most trustworthy mages, and everything in between. This controversy would come to a head during the splintering of Khetapera, when it became a dividing line between the newly independent cities, which in turn would serve as justification for war between them. To avoid similar conflicts in the future, we need to use our authority as Stewards of Kheterata to hand down the definitive interpretation of the Decree, so that there can be no future doubt on the proper use of the divine gift.

  • All power costs: -2.5% (all_power_cost; raw value -0.025).

6. Expand the Southern Brotherhoods

In the south of Kheterata, the Ahati serve a somewhat different role than they do in the north. As the merchants of the south needed protection from gnollish raids, and the Ahati wished for further autonomy from Kheterat, the two would eventually join together, forming trade guilds ruled by the Ahati code of honor. We weren’t aware of what a blessing this was until the splintering of Kheterata, when much of the treacherous northern merchant class threw their lot in with the heathen pretenders of Elizna. Such blasphemous treachery is unacceptable in Prakheta. It is clear that we need to expand the system of Ahati merchant guilds to all of The Sorrow, so that the northern merchants may finally learn some honor and discipline.

  • Domestic trade power: +10% (global_own_trade_power; raw value 0.1).

7. Bring Order to Horashesh

Perhaps the most impressive feat of the Crodamics before their downfall was just how far they managed to spread the light of the Khet. Their domain from sea to sea, possessing fleets in both Koroshesh in the north and Zuvavim in the south. But the great distance from Kheterat to Horashesh, further separated by the mountains of Khetapera, made it impossible for the Stewards to directly manage the region. Instead, they relied on a system of appointed governors ruling the local satrapies alongside local rulers. This proved disastrous for the region once Grizaka cut off the path from Horashesh to Kheterat. With no royal aid to keep the governors in line and help them enforce order, all of Horashesh quickly descended into chaos, with both governors turning on each other and the local kings scrambling to usurp power from the royal governors. Luckily, with our capital much further south, we can govern the region in a more direct and unified manner. The Horasheshi can rest easy knowing that unlike the previous Kheterata, we will never lose control over their land.

  • Core-creation cost: -5% (core_creation; raw value -0.05).

  • global_autonomy: -0.025% (global_autonomy; raw value -0.025).

Prakhetan Ambitions

  • Free Administrative Policies: +1 (free_adm_policy; raw value 1).
